body:
It would strictly speaking need double checking that existing `find` cases don't rely on negative `p_from` returning -1, this is compat breaking behaviour as you say.

In 99% coding uses I'd (personally) rather have it flag up that a negative `p_from` was being passed, as it was likely a bug on the calling side. Now it will work transparently and produce a "viable" result, potentially making this kind of bug harder to track down (although admittedly already it returns -1, which is difficult to detect).

I guess the calling code could put in a check for negative if required, and sometimes a hard check is better like a `DEV_ASSERT()` or `ERR_FAIL_COND()`, and that kind of choice wouldn't be available in the function itself anyway.

The PR is probably a reasonable compromise imo, but see what others think.

> It would strictly speaking need double checking that existing `find` cases don't rely on negative `p_from` returning -1, this is compat breaking behaviour as you say.

Yes, admittedly I haven't done that. I'll follow up.

> In 99% coding uses I'd (personally) rather have it flag up that a negative `p_from` was being passed, as it was likely a bug on the calling side. Now it will work transparently and produce a "viable" result, potentially making this kind of bug harder to track down (although admittedly already it returns -1, which is difficult to detect).

As a data scientist I'm very used to negative indices, and use them in code regularly. It's just a nice shortcut to be able to omit `array.size()` if you index regularly. It's admittedly less important in games, and could definitely be confusing to new users. But now we kinda have the worst of both worlds, where it works sometimes but doesn't other times 😅

> I guess the calling code could put in a check for negative if required, and sometimes a hard check is better like a `DEV_ASSERT()` or `ERR_FAIL_COND()`, and that kind of choice wouldn't be available in the function itself anyway.

I do like this idea too.
Perhaps the best compromise is actually no compromise at all. Simply remove the `p_from` parameter and force callers to handle indexing logic (by creating subspans). It's a bit of duplicate logic, but arguably it's correctly duplicate logic. And the user facing callers could add the error checks you're suggesting.
It would be good for callers anyway that call `find` repeatedly, under the general umbrella of 'you don't pay for what you don't use'.
I think i'll toy around with this and see how it feels. The main downside would be that callers of `Span` would have to be aware it's got fewer helping comforts than the outer `Vector`, `String` and `LocalVector` implementations.

Edit: I have tested erroring out. It turns out it's not possible to be consistent with it - if you test for negative or `>= size()` starting indexes, you'll have a special case for `size() == 0 && p_from ==0`, where you're explicitly ignoring emitting an error here. That's very unsatisfying.
